title: Monetary Incentives and Knowledge Spillover: Evidence from a Natural Experiment
authors: Jing Wang; Gen Li; Kai-Lung Hui
near_miss_reason: Staggered setting (Zhihu users first host a paid Live talk in months 0-23 after the May 2016 launch; 24 distinct first_month values, never-host comparison users), but the authors never estimate a pooled staggered TWFE. Every main-text DiD (Table 2 and Tables 3, 4, 6-11, Figure 7; codes/Table2-...-main.txt) is a batch-specific regression: hosts whose first talk falls in one six-month window (G1: months 0-5, G2: 6-11, G3: 12-17, G4: 18-23) vs CEM-matched non-hosts, with after = test_month >= window start, i.e., a single common onset per regression (cohort-by-cohort 2x2), and every column is weighted by CEM weights (xtreg ... [pweight=cem_answer_amount_weights], fe). CEM analytic weights are excluded (5c ruling, mnsc.2020.03920), so the columns fail both the staggered-timing rule and the weighting rule. The only individual-date version (Appendix Table B1) is appendix-only, CEM-weighted, assigns random pseudo adoption dates to non-hosts and restricts each unit to its own +/-6-month window. The pooled version (Appendix Table E1) uses one common date (test_month >= 0).
eligible_reason: Not eligible as reported. Each main-text regression is xtreg log_y did i.test_month [pweight=cem_answer_amount_weights] if window, fe with did = treatment x after and after = 1{test_month >= batch start} (0, 6, 12 or 18), so all treated users in a regression share one onset date even though their first live talks are spread over six months; the four batches are estimated separately (not stacked, not pooled). All DiD columns use CEM weights. Table 9-11 long-term specifications add four did1-did4 period interactions within the same single-onset batch structure; Table 6/H3/G1/H6 split or interact by reputation and fee subgroups; Table 3 is a placebo with a fake onset. Poisson FE (xtpoisson) columns are also reported. No column satisfies every rule.
design_notes: User-month panel (answer_panel_adlink.dta: 565,998 rows, 6,086 users = 2,024 hosts + 4,062 non-hosts after dropping organization accounts; test_month -65..27, month 0 = May 14-June 13, 2016). Outcomes: log answers, log characters per answer, log vote-ups per answer (and article analogues in Table A1). CEM on pre-period answer quantity, length, vote-ups and tenure. xtreg fe with pweights implies user-clustered SEs. A Hull-comparable staggered design could be built from first_month (24 monthly cohorts, never-hosts as controls), but it is not a reported specification.

screener_notes: Screened from package (readme.txt, all code .txt files, data) and the OpenAlex abstract (CEM + DiD, 9.4%-40.8% more answers). No article text or PDF; table numbering is taken from the code file names and readme. Excluded from 5c as well, because the violation is CEM weighting and single-onset batching, not time-varying controls.
